verdicts.claim: By default SQLite runs one automatically from the committing connection once the WAL equals or exceeds 1000 pages ... and again when the last connection closes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages' and last closing connection 'does one last checkpoint'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE does what RESTART does and then truncates the WAL to zero bytes. FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE hold the writer lock and block new writers
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'; 'blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded'

verdicts.claim: If another process is already checkpointing, the call returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately and the busy-handler is not invoked even if one is configured
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row of three integers: busy ..., frames in the WAL, frames checkpointed. The last two are -1 when there is no WAL
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'returns a single row with three integer columns' ... 'The second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'. (The 'both are 0 after TRUNCATE' sub-clause is not stated verbatim.)

verdicts.claim: Under PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL the checkpoint is the only operation that syncs
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation' with writers omitting sync under NORMAL

verdicts.claim: Litestream ... holds a long-running read transaction ... Earlier v0.3.x releases used generation IDs and shadow WAL files; v0.5 replaced both with TXID-based LTX
verdicts.evidence: how-it-works: 'starts a long-running read transaction to prevent any other process from checkpointing'; 'Litestream v0.5 replaces both concepts with TXID-based LTX files.'

verdicts.claim: Litestream v0.5.x three-tier policy: min-checkpoint-page-count (1000 pages, ~4 MB, PASSIVE), checkpoint-interval (1m), truncate-page-n (121359, ~500 MB); since v0.5.15 PASSIVE first
verdicts.evidence: guide: 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default: ~4MB', 'checkpoint-interval: 1m', 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB', 'first attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint'; 'truncate-page-n: 0' disables

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug ... affects 3.7.0 through 3.51.2; fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and 3.53.0 (2026-04-09), with backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09)... fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)'; backports 3.44.6, 3.50.7 listed; news 3.53.0 (2026-04-09): 'The WAL-reset bug is fixed in this release.'

verdicts.claim: 3.52.0, which carried the first fix, was withdrawn
verdicts.evidence: news.html 3.51.3 entry: 'SQLite version 3.52.0 has been withdrawn'; 3.52.0 entry: 'A 15-year-old database corruption bug ... is now fixed.'

verdicts.claim: Syncthing hit [checkpoint starvation] during large folder syncs where database activity is nearly constant
verdicts.evidence: forum (bt90, 2026-02-06): 'There is almost constant reading/writing to the database.'; also 'As checkpoints of any kind are exclusive, we're blocking our own checkpointer.'

Draft's Disagreement bullet about backports confirmed: news.html lists no 3.44.6 or 3.50.7 entries (3.44 series up to 3.44.2, 3.50 up to 3.50.4); only wal.html names them.
